title: Learn More
subtitle: Discover the essentials of lawn bowls, how to get started, and where to go next.

body: Whether you're completely new or looking to improve, this is your starting point.

sections.alt: A woman in club whites and a wide-brimmed sun hat standing on the mat at the end of a lawn bowls green, holding a yellow bowl up in one hand

items.title: What is Lawn Bowls?
items.body: A precision sport where players roll biased bowls to get closest to the jack. Simple to learn, challenging to master.

items.title: Getting Started
items.body: Visit a local club, try a session, and connect with experienced players who can guide you.

items.title: Equipment Basics
items.body: Bowls, jack, and flat-soled shoes are the essentials. Most clubs provide equipment for beginners.

items.title: Types of Games
items.body: Singles, pairs, triples, and fours — each format offers different strategies and team dynamics.

items.title: Improve Your Game
items.body: Coaching sessions, drills, and competitive play help develop consistency and decision-making.

items.title: Join the Community
items.body: Lawn bowls is as social as it is competitive — meet players, join events, and become part of the network.

migrationNotes: The source page has no body images. The only content image was a CSS background photo behind the hero banner (IMG_3223 Large.jpeg); it has been saved as 01-hero-green.jpg and carried across as a standalone image section, since the schema has no hero-background type.
The 'Watch videos →' link sat inside the 'Improve Your Game' card. It is kept both as that card's link and as a standalone button so it is not lost in renderers that ignore card links.
The page's visual design (dark green gradient hero, six-card grid, hover effects) is Squarespace code-block CSS and is not carried across — the shared page.html template supplies the styling.

The page carries no dates, committee names or contact details, so there is nothing time-sensitive to check. All three links (/coachinghub, /club-info, the Southwest Lawn Bowls YouTube channel) were live at migration time.
